content: In Romans, Paul says God works all things together for the good of whom?
explanation: They are called by His purpose. “And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him” (Romans 8:28, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says God works how many things together for good?
explanation: Even hard times are in His hands. “God works all things together for the good” (Romans 8:28, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: Complete Paul's words to the Romans: “If God is for us, who can be…”
explanation: No one can defeat God's people. “If God is for us, who can be against us?” (Romans 8:31, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says that in all troubles we are more than what?
explanation: It is through Him who loved us. “No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.” (Romans 8:37, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says nothing in all creation can separate us from what?
explanation: God's love in Christ holds us fast. “will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” (Romans 8:39, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says the Spirit helps us when we don't know how to do what?
explanation: The Spirit intercedes for us. “For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us” (Romans 8:26, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says there is now no condemnation for those who are where?
explanation: Jesus took our punishment. “Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” (Romans 8:1, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul says the Spirit testifies with our spirit that we are what?
explanation: We belong to God's family. “The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.” (Romans 8:16, BSB)
tags: All Things Work Together for Good

content: In Romans, Paul writes that all have sinned and fall short of what?
explanation: Everyone needs God's grace. “for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says God proved His love because Christ died for us while we were what?
explanation: God loved us first. “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is what?
explanation: It comes in Christ Jesus our Lord. “For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” (Romans 6:23, BSB)

content: In Romans, what does Paul say we must confess with our mouth to be saved?
explanation: And believe God raised Him. “that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,”” (Romans 10:9, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be what?
explanation: The promise is for everyone. “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.” (Romans 10:13, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul quotes, “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring…”
explanation: Preachers must be sent. “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!” (Romans 10:15, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says faith comes by what?
explanation: Hearing comes through the word of Christ. “Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.” (Romans 10:17, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul urges believers to offer their bodies as what?
explanation: That is true worship. “to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God” (Romans 12:1, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says be transformed by the renewing of what?
explanation: Do not copy this world. “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.” (Romans 12:2, BSB)

content: In Romans, how does Paul tell believers to overcome evil?
explanation: Do not let evil win. “Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” (Romans 12:21, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says rejoice with those who rejoice and do what with those who weep?
explanation: Share in others' feelings. “Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.” (Romans 12:15, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and persistent in what?
explanation: Keep praying in every season. “Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.” (Romans 12:12, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says that in Christ we who are many are one what?
explanation: Each member belongs to the others. “so in Christ we who are many are one body” (Romans 12:5, BSB)

content: In Romans, what does Paul call the fulfillment of the law?
explanation: Love does no wrong to a neighbor. “Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.” (Romans 13:10, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says he is not ashamed of what?
explanation: It is God's power for salvation. “I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation” (Romans 1:16, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul quotes that who believed God and was counted righteous?
explanation: Faith was credited as righteousness. “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.” (Romans 4:3, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says that since we are justified through faith, we have what with God?
explanation: It comes through our Lord Jesus Christ. “we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” (Romans 5:1, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul quotes that no one is what, not even one?
explanation: All need a Savior. “There is no one righteous, not even one.” (Romans 3:10, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says, if possible, live at peace with whom?
explanation: Do your part for peace. “If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.” (Romans 12:18, BSB)

content: To believers in which city did Paul write the letter of Romans?
explanation: They were loved by God. “To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints” (Romans 1:7, BSB)

content: Who wrote down Paul's letter to the Romans for him?
explanation: He added his own greeting. “I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.” (Romans 16:22, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul commends Phoebe, a servant of the church in which place?
explanation: She likely carried the letter. “I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.” (Romans 16:1, BSB)

content: In Romans, what word does Paul say we cry out to God by the Spirit of sonship?
explanation: We are God's adopted children. “by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”” (Romans 8:15, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says suffering produces perseverance, which produces what?
explanation: Character then produces hope. “perseverance, character; and character, hope.” (Romans 5:4, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says we were buried with Christ through baptism so we may walk in what?
explanation: Christ was raised from the dead. “we too may walk in newness of life.” (Romans 6:4, BSB)

content: In Romans, which couple does Paul greet as his fellow workers?
explanation: They were tentmakers like Paul. “Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus” (Romans 16:3, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says God's children are co-heirs with whom?
explanation: We share in His glory. “heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ” (Romans 8:17, BSB)

content: In Romans, Paul says present sufferings cannot compare to what?
explanation: Hope looks forward. “I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.” (Romans 8:18, BSB)
